harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/legacy2/stale-pidfile-startup/bin/control on node1. It now safely distinguishes live, stale, foreign, and missing PID states; serializes concurrent actions; preserves a single worker; and never signals unrelated processes. The existing journal was preserved. Node1 was safely restarted once and recovered on the unchanged RHEL 7.9 / 3.10 kernel.
actions_performed: Installed a POSIX-compatible control script using the platform's existing Python and flock utilities.
Verified stale-PID recovery, live worker handling, foreign-process protection, and idempotent stop behavior.
Verified sequential and concurrent repeated starts retain exactly one worker.
Preserved journal inode 50762688 and its original B100 entry while allowing normal ticks to append.
Restarted node1 exactly once, confirmed its boot identity changed, and recovered the worker from the reboot-stale PID file.

evidence.requirement: Start, stop, and status distinguish live workers, stale PIDs, and PIDs belonging to other processes without harming unrelated processes.
evidence.summary: Live stop removed the worker; stale status returned 1 and cleaned safely; foreign status returned 2; foreign PID 2560 remained alive across control start and stop; post-reboot stale PID 2753 was recognized and replaced by worker 1050.

evidence.requirement: Repeated starts retain a single worker.
evidence.summary: Sequential starts retained PID 2385 with worker_count=1. Three concurrent starts all returned success and converged on PID 2753 with worker_count=1.
Journal inode 50762688 and the original 'previous worker completed batch B100' entry remained intact before and after testing and restart; only normal tick records were appended.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged. The repair uses /bin/sh, existing Python, procfs, and existing flock.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data.
evidence.summary: Before restart, worker 2753 was healthy with worker_count=1 under boot b35fad86-4e61-46bf-bbd2-0dadcedb685d. Safe reboot acknowledgement was captured. The new boot identity is a38b2014-1f58-4204-b69f-992d346f88b1. After restart, the control script recovered the stale PID, worker 1050 was healthy with worker_count=1, checksums persisted, and the journal remained intact.
